record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: A finite set X is sphere-Ramsey if, for every number of colors r, there exist a dimension N and a radius ρ such that every r-coloring of the sphere S^N(ρ) contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X. If X is Ramsey in Euclidean space, must X also be sphere-Ramsey?

Conjecture 7 ($1000). If X is Ramsey then X is sphere-Ramsey.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set X ⊂ ℝ^n and a positive integer r, say that X is Ramsey if there exists a positive integer N such that every r-coloring of ℝ^N contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X. Say that X is sphere-Ramsey if for every positive integer r there exist a positive integer N and a positive real number ρ such that every r-coloring of the sphere S^N(ρ) = {x ∈ ℝ^{N+1} : |x| = ρ} contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X.

Prove or disprove: every finite Ramsey set X ⊂ ℝ^n is sphere-Ramsey.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every Ramsey set is sphere-Ramsey is part of the well-known set of open conjectures in Euclidean Ramsey theory (with a $1000 prize attached by Graham). Surveys and recent works (e.g., Leader–Russell–Walters on transitive sets, Graham's surveys) treat it as an outstanding open problem; no resolution has been reported.
